items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee (Monk Montgomery) narrates that his brother Buddy talked to Mildred Thompson (the club owner) and that she was delighted to have them play, but Monk himself does not describe a direct personal interaction or relationship with her.

ctx.x: It was called the Turf Bar, and these people were going bankrupt. Nice people, but they were going bankrupt. They had a duet, working the club, where the lady played organ and her husband played drums, and that's what the entertainment was like. And the place was dying; they were going bankrupt.

He talked to this lady, Mildred Thompson was the proprietor there, said, 'What you should do, Mildred, is bring in a black group, would turn the whole thing around.' Well, you know, they ain't gonna...She was thinking, like, well, see...
We were back in that period in time when she was afraid to bring in a black group because she thought it might attract some black trade, or something, and you can't do that.
